## Professional career
### 2022
Watt during training camp in 2022
In Week 1 against the Bengals, Watt left the game in the fourth quarter with a torn pectoral muscle during the 23–20 overtime win, after attempting to sack quarterback Joe Burrow.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-134) He was placed on injured reserve.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-135)
On October 8, it was reported that Watt had recently undergone arthroscopic knee surgery for an injury sustained in the preseason.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-136) On October 26, the Steelers opened the 21-day practice window for Watt's return.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-137) He was activated from injured reserve on November 11, 2022.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-138)
He finished the 2022 season with 39 tackles, two interceptions, one forced fumble, and a career low 5.5 sacks in 10 games played.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-renamed_from_2023_on_20231207154808-139) Despite this, Watt was voted to his fifth consecutive Pro Bowl.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-140)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-141) After the season, Watt was ranked 27th on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2023.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-142)

## Professional career
### 2023
In Week 1, a 30–7 loss to the 49ers, Watt would serve as one of the few bright spots for the Steelers as he sacked 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy three times, two of which resulted in forced fumbles. In addition, his three sacks brought his career total to 80.5, tying the Steelers franchise record set by James Harrison.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-143)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-144) In Week 2, Watt broke Harrison's franchise sack record by sacking Deshaun Watson and bringing his career total to 81.5. Watt later recovered a Watson fumble forced by teammate Alex Highsmith and returned it 17 yards for the game-winning touchdown in the 26–22 victory over the Browns.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-145)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-146) For his strong performance in the first three games of the season, Watt was named AFC Defensive Player of the Month for September.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-147) On January 2, 2024, the Steelers named Watt Team MVP for the fourth time. He is now tied with Antonio Brown in that category.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-148) In Week 18, Watt would record two sacks in the season finale versus the Ravens before leaving the game late in the third quarter with a Grade 2 MCL sprain.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-149) This brought his total to 19 sacks on the year, the second time he has reached that total, (only his brother J. J. Watt, DeMarcus Ware, and Mark Gastineau have reached that mark twice).

## Professional career
### 2023
He also became the first player to lead the NFL in sacks three times, since sacks became an official stat in 1982.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-150)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-CBSS2023-151) For his performance in Week 18, Watt was named AFC Defensive Player of the Week after recording eight tackles (six solo), two sacks, and three tackles for loss.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-152) He finished the 2023 season with 68 tackles, 19 sacks, four forced fumbles, one interception, and one defensive touchdown.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-153) He was voted to his sixth Pro Bowl, and was named first-team All-Pro for a fourth time.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-154)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-155)
On January 15, 2024, Watt was inactive for the Steelers playoff game against the Bills due to a knee injury.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-Irving-156) The Steelers lost the game, 31–17, and were eliminated from the playoffs in the Wild Card Round.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-157) Following the season, Watt's fellow players voted him eighth on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2024.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-p931-158)

In Week 1, a 30–7 loss to the 49ers, Watt would serve as one of the few bright spots for the Steelers as he sacked 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy three times, two of which resulted in forced fumbles. Watt later recovered a Watson fumble forced by teammate Alex Highsmith and returned it 17 yards for the game-winning touchdown in the 26–22 victory over the Browns.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-145)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-146) For his strong performance in the first three games of the season, Watt was named AFC Defensive Player of the Month for September.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-147) On January 2, 2024, the Steelers named Watt Team MVP for the fourth time. He is now tied with Antonio Brown in that category.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-148) In Week 18, Watt would record two sacks in the season finale versus the Ravens before leaving the game late in the third quarter with a Grade 2 MCL sprain.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._J._Watt#cite_note-149) This brought his total to 19 sacks on the year, the second time he has reached that total, (only his brother J. J. Watt, DeMarcus Ware, and Mark Gastineau have reached that mark twice).
